lesson_01.prompt: Which HTTP method should be used when a cloud client dispatches a new navigation goal to the robot API gateway?
options: GET
POST
PUT
HEAD
lesson_01.explanation: POST is used to create new resources and dispatch stateful actions with a JSON body. GET must be idempotent and read-only without modifying robot state.

lesson_01.prompt: Which HTTP status code is most appropriate for acknowledging an asynchronous navigation dispatch that will execute over the next several seconds?
options: 200 OK
202 Accepted
204 No Content
301 Moved Permanently
lesson_01.explanation: HTTP 202 Accepted indicates that the request has been received and validated, but processing has not yet completed—standard for long-running robotics actions.

lesson_02.prompt: Why is persistent WebSocket streaming vastly superior to HTTP polling for streaming 20Hz AMR telemetry to web cockpits?
options: WebSockets do not use TCP sockets
WebSockets establish a single persistent TCP connection with only 2 to 6 bytes of framing overhead per message, avoiding repeated HTTP handshake latency and header bloat
HTTP polling cannot transmit JSON data
WebSockets bypass Linux network permissions
lesson_02.explanation: HTTP polling sends ~800 bytes of headers on every single request and introduces TCP connection overhead. WebSockets maintain a full-duplex socket with microsecond latency and tiny 2-byte frame headers.

lesson_03.prompt: In an enterprise robotics Dual-Plane Architecture, what is the fundamental boundary between the Real-Time Control Plane and Application Plane?
options: The Real-Time Plane runs deterministic motor control loops and safety guards without network blocking, while the Application Plane handles cloud networking, REST/WebSockets, and AI logic asynchronously
The Real-Time Plane runs on Windows while the Application Plane runs on Linux
The Real-Time Plane only runs in Gazebo simulation
There is no boundary; everything executes inside a single Python thread
lesson_03.explanation: Dual-Plane Architecture isolates safety-critical control (wheel velocity loops, emergency stops, LiDAR processing) from non-deterministic external networks and LLM agent delays.

lesson_04.prompt: Which ROS 2 callback group must be assigned to service servers and subscriptions in a MultiThreadedExecutor to allow concurrent execution without blocking each other?
options: MutuallyExclusiveCallbackGroup
ReentrantCallbackGroup
StaticCallbackGroup
AsyncCallbackGroup
lesson_04.explanation: ReentrantCallbackGroup allows callbacks in that group to execute in parallel across multiple worker threads. MutuallyExclusiveCallbackGroup restricts execution to one thread at a time.

lesson_05.prompt: Why is Pydantic v2 used to define data schemas in FastAPI robotics gateways?
options: It compiles Python into C++ binaries
It enforces strict runtime data validation, automatic type coercion, bounds checking, and generates OpenAPI documentation automatically
It replaces rclpy entirely
It allows direct access to CAN bus hardware
lesson_05.explanation: Pydantic validates incoming client payloads (e.g. verifying coordinates are finite numbers within [-50, 50]), rejecting malformed JSON before it can corrupt robot nodes.

lesson_06.prompt: What pattern should be used in a Python WebSocket broadcaster to handle multiple connected frontend cockpits cleanly?
options: A ConnectionManager class tracking active WebSocket connections in a set and broadcasting JSON concurrently via asyncio.gather()
Spawning a separate Linux process for each browser tab
Blocking the main thread with a while True loop
Opening a separate port for every client
lesson_06.explanation: A ConnectionManager manages connected client sockets, discards dead connections gracefully upon disconnect, and broadcasts serialized telemetry using asynchronous tasks.

lesson_07.prompt: How does an asynchronous FastAPI route handler interact with a ROS 2 ActionClient without blocking the uvicorn event loop?
options: By calling send_goal_async() and awaiting a Future / asyncio Event bridge
By invoking time.sleep(10)
By running colcon build inside the route
By restarting the uvicorn daemon
lesson_07.explanation: send_goal_async() returns an rclpy Future. By hooking this future into the asyncio event loop, the web server remains responsive to health checks and E-Stop requests.

lesson_08.prompt: When an Emergency Stop endpoint (/api/v1/emergency_stop) is triggered on the API Gateway, what must happen immediately?
options: The robot continues to its goal and stops afterwards
The gateway publishes zero velocities to /cmd_vel, latches an internal safety lock, and rejects all subsequent navigation requests until an explicit reset
The container terminates
The LiDAR sensor is powered off
lesson_08.explanation: Safety latching guarantees immediate velocity dampening to zero and blocks new navigation commands from being accepted until an authorized reset occurs.

lesson_09.prompt: What resilience mechanism should a robotics client SDK implement for its WebSocket telemetry connection?
options: Automatic exponential backoff reconnection with heartbeat ping/pong monitoring
Immediate process crash upon packet drop
Switching automatically to HTTP polling permanently
Disabling SSL verification
lesson_09.explanation: AMRs frequently roam across Wi-Fi access points. Client SDKs must implement exponential backoff reconnection and heartbeat monitoring to recover instantly from transient disconnects.

lesson_10.prompt: Why is an HTML5 2D Canvas preferred over DOM div elements for rendering industrial fleet cockpits?
options: DOM elements cannot show colors
A single Canvas uses hardware-accelerated GPU draw calls (requestAnimationFrame) to render thousands of map cells, laser points, and robot poses at 60 FPS without DOM reflow overhead
Canvas does not support JavaScript
Canvas requires Node.js
lesson_10.explanation: DOM nodes create memory overhead and layout thrashing. The Canvas 2D API renders directly to a bitmap buffer using GPU acceleration, easily maintaining 60 FPS.

lesson_11.prompt: In a 2D SLAM OccupancyGrid, what do cell values of -1, 0, and 100 represent?
options: -1 = Unknown space, 0 = Free space, 100 = Lethal obstacle / Wall
-1 = Wall, 0 = Unknown, 100 = Free
-1 = Battery empty, 0 = Idle, 100 = Moving
-1 = Error, 0 = Ground, 100 = Sky
lesson_11.explanation: ROS 2 OccupancyGrid standard: -1 indicates unmapped/unknown space, 0 represents verified traversable free space, and 100 represents a lethal occupied obstacle.

lesson_12.prompt: How do you render a robot pose heading indicator on a Canvas with world coordinates (x, y, yaw)?
options: ctx.save(), ctx.translate(pixelX, pixelY), ctx.rotate(-yaw), draw heading vector, ctx.restore()
By changing CSS font-size
By reloading the entire canvas image
By sending an HTTP request to the browser
lesson_12.explanation: The 2D transform pipeline (save -> translate -> rotate -> draw -> restore) isolates rotation math to the robot icon without altering the world map coordinate system.

lesson_13.prompt: Why should a virtual teleoperation joystick implement a 'deadband' zone near the center position?
options: To increase maximum robot speed
To prevent jitter, tiny touch inaccuracies, and sensor drift from commanding accidental creeping movement when the stick is near center
To save battery power when driving backwards
To disable emergency stop
lesson_13.explanation: A deadband (e.g. 10% radius) ensures that minor finger twitches or touch release residual positions do not send non-zero velocity commands to the robot base.

lesson_14.prompt: What coordinate system should map landmark waypoints be stored in?
options: Screen pixel coordinates (clientX, clientY)
Metric world coordinates in the global 'map' frame (x, y, yaw in meters and radians)
Local odometry coordinates relative to base_link
GPS latitude and longitude only
lesson_14.explanation: Screen pixels vary with screen size and zoom levels. Storing metric poses in the 'map' frame ensures persistent, device-independent navigation accuracy.

lesson_15.prompt: What security header should be configured on the FastAPI gateway to prevent unauthorized web applications from accessing robot control endpoints?
options: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) headers specifying explicit allowed origins
Content-Security-Policy set to none
X-Frame-Options set to true
Server header set to ROS2
lesson_15.explanation: CORSMiddleware allows specifying explicit trusted origins (e.g. https://fleet.botforge.in), preventing malicious third-party websites from making cross-origin control requests.

lesson_16.prompt: In the Day 2 Capstone Web Cockpit, how are operator click-to-navigate coordinates converted into world coordinates?
options: By dividing screen width by 2
Using the inverse canvas transformation matrix: worldX = (screenX - panX) / scale, worldY = -(screenY - panY) / scale
By calling navigator.geolocation
By reading the robot's odometer
lesson_16.explanation: Inverse transformation maps screen viewport coordinates back into metric meters, accounting for pan offsets, canvas scaling, and the Y-axis inversion between screen and Cartesian coordinates.

lesson_17.prompt: What is 'Physical Grounding' in the context of robotics AI agents?
options: Connecting the robot's metal chassis to electrical earth ground
Translating abstract semantic human language ('Inspect cargo rack B') into verified metric coordinates, physical safety bounds, and valid ROS 2 actions
Training neural networks on physical GPUs
Preventing the robot wheels from slipping
lesson_17.explanation: Grounded reasoning bridges the gap between probabilistic LLM tokens and deterministic physical reality, mapping concepts like 'Shelf 3' to metric poses verified against obstacle maps.

lesson_18.prompt: What protocol specification does the Model Context Protocol (MCP) use for client-server communication?
options: gRPC over HTTP/2
JSON-RPC 2.0 with standard methods (tools/list, tools/call, resources/list)
Raw TCP sockets
GraphQL
lesson_18.explanation: MCP standardizes AI tool use via JSON-RPC 2.0. Clients (Claude, Gemini, Antigravity) discover tools via tools/list and invoke deterministic robotics actions via tools/call.

lesson_19.prompt: In an MCP Robotics Server, why must tools provide strict JSON Schema definitions in 'inputSchema'?
options: So the LLM understands expected parameter names, types, constraints, and required fields before generating tool calls
To speed up colcon build
To format console print outputs
To encrypt network traffic
lesson_19.explanation: The inputSchema guides the LLM's function-calling engine, ensuring arguments adhere strictly to required types (e.g. float between -50 and 50) and avoiding hallucinations.

lesson_20.prompt: Why must deterministic safety guards be implemented in software BEFORE executing an AI agent's navigation tool call?
options: Because LLMs can hallucinate unsafe coordinates, violate geofence boundaries, or command actions when battery is critically low
Because Python requires pre-checks to allocate memory
Because ROS 2 nodes cannot handle numbers greater than 100
Because DDS crashes if a target is unreachable
lesson_20.explanation: LLMs are probabilistic and cannot be solely trusted with physical safety. Hard deterministic guards (geofences, speed clamps, battery interlocks) enforce non-negotiable physical constraints.

lesson_21.prompt: Which transport mechanism does the Model Context Protocol support for running local AI agents on the same host as the robot?
options: Standard Input/Output (stdio) JSON-RPC streams
Bluetooth Low Energy
RS-232 Serial
NFC
lesson_21.explanation: MCP supports stdio transport where the agent process spawns the server as a child process and communicates via standard input/output pipes with zero network overhead.

lesson_22.prompt: What is the defining property of a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) in robotics mission workflow planning?
options: The graph contains directed edges and has no closed loops, ensuring a deterministic sequence of tasks with clear dependencies and completion criteria
The graph can only have a single node
All nodes must execute in parallel
The graph resets when power is lost
lesson_22.explanation: A DAG guarantees execution flow without infinite dependency deadlocks. Each node has clear prerequisites and predictable progression toward mission completion.

lesson_23.prompt: How does a 'HumanApprovalGate' step function in a stateful mission execution graph?
options: It terminates the mission immediately
It pauses mission progression, presents a prompt/alert to an operator via web or edge badge, and waits for explicit approval before resuming autonomous execution
It overrides the robot's LiDAR sensors
It prompts the operator for a root password
lesson_23.explanation: Interaction gates provide human-in-the-loop oversight for high-risk actions (e.g. entering restricted zones or operating heavy actuators), ensuring safety before proceeding.

lesson_24.prompt: In the Day 3 Grand Capstone, what is the full end-to-end data pipeline from human operator prompt to physical AMR execution?
options: Natural Language Prompt -> Frontier AI Model (MCP Agent) -> Validated Mission DAG -> FastAPI Gateway -> ROS 2 Nav2 Execution & Telemetry Feedback
Prompt -> Bash script -> Hardware reboot
ROS 2 Topic -> Gazebo -> Web browser -> Python script
FastAPI -> SQLite -> Docker restart
lesson_24.explanation: The architecture seamlessly unites physical AI: Natural language is parsed by the LLM agent via MCP, compiled into a validated DAG mission, dispatched via the API Gateway, executed by Nav2, and monitored on the web cockpit.
